records.source: בָּנִ֣ים אַתֶּ֔ם לַֽיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֑ם לֹ֣א תִתְגֹּֽדְד֗וּ וְלֹֽא־תָשִׂ֧ימוּ קָרְחָ֛ה בֵּ֥ין עֵינֵיכֶ֖ם לָמֵֽת׃
records.gloss: Sons [are] you of Yahweh your God; not you will cut yourselves, and not you will make baldness between your eyes for [the] dead.
pieces: You are {{gender:children|sons}} of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. Do not gash yourselves or shave a bald patch on your foreheads in mourning for the dead.

L.1: You [are] {{gender:children|sons}} of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. You shall not cut yourselves, and you shall not make a bald spot between your eyes for the dead.

R.1: You are the {{gender:children|sons}} of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. So when someone dies, do not cut your bodies or shave the front of your heads to show your sorrow.

decisions.choice: children of the LORD your God: Israel belongs to God as a family belongs to its father
decisions.reason: The word is "sons", but it is said of the whole people, men and women. God called Israel his firstborn son (Exodus 4:22), and Moses has said that the LORD trains Israel as a father trains his son (8:5; compare 1:31; 32:5-6; Hosea 11:1). Moses is still speaking in the speech that began at 5:1. Because the people belong to God in this way, they must not take up the mourning customs of the peoples around them; verse 2 gives the reason in full.

decisions.choice: cut yourselves, make a bald spot for the dead: rites of mourning practiced by Israel's neighbors
decisions.reason: Gashing the body and shaving part of the head were known signs of grief in the ancient world (Isaiah 15:2; Jeremiah 16:6; 41:5; 47:5), and the prophets of Baal cut themselves in worship (1 Kings 18:28). Leviticus forbids the same rites to all Israel and to the priests (Leviticus 19:27-28; 21:5). The law does not forbid grief; it forbids marking the body in the way the nations did.

decisions.choice: between your eyes: on the forehead, the front of the head above the eyes
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used for the place where the words of God are to be worn as a sign (6:8; 11:18). Here it names the front of the scalp, which was shaved bare in mourning.

decisions.choice: on your foreheads; in mourning for the dead / when someone dies ... to show your sorrow
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say where "between your eyes" is and that these rites were signs of grief, as Leviticus 19:28 does. Literal keeps "between your eyes for the dead".

records.heading: Children of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}

records.source: כִּ֣י עַ֤ם קָדוֹשׁ֙ אַתָּ֔ה לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ וּבְךָ֞ בָּחַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה לִֽהְי֥וֹת לוֹ֙ לְעַ֣ם סְגֻלָּ֔ה מִכֹּל֙ הָֽעַמִּ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: For a people holy [are] you to Yahweh your God, and you has chosen Yahweh to be for him for a people of treasured possession out of all the peoples which [are] on [the] face of the ground.
pieces: For you are a people set apart as holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. Out of all the peoples on the face of the earth, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has chosen you to be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own special treasure.

L.2: For you [are] a holy people to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has chosen you to be a people of special possession for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} out of all the peoples that [are] on the face of the ground.

R.2: You belong to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God as a holy people. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} chose you out of all the nations on earth to be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own special treasure.

decisions.choice: for: the reason for verse 1, and the ground of the food laws that follow
decisions.reason: Israel must not mourn as the nations do because it is a holy people. The same words return in verse 21 to close the food laws, so this sentence stands over the whole section: what Israel does with its body and what it eats both show whose people it is.

decisions.choice: a holy people: a people set apart as belonging to God
decisions.reason: To be holy is to be set apart for God and so marked off from what is common or unclean (Exodus 19:6; Leviticus 11:44-45). Here it is not a reward for good conduct but a fact God has made true by choosing Israel; the commands that follow show how Israel is to live as what it already is (7:6; 26:19).

decisions.choice: a people of special possession: a personal treasure, prized and owned
decisions.reason: The word is used of a king's own store of treasure (1 Chronicles 29:2-3; Ecclesiastes 2:8). God uses it of Israel in Exodus 19:5 and Deuteronomy 7:6 and 26:18, and 1 Peter 2:9 takes it up. The verse is almost word for word the same as 7:6.

decisions.choice: you (singular): the people addressed as one
decisions.reason: Verse 1 speaks to the people with plural verbs; here the address turns singular, as Deuteronomy often does, because Israel is one people before God. The meaning does not change.

decisions.choice: own special treasure
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 19:5, Balanced and Readable say "own special treasure" to bring out both ownership and value; Literal has "special possession".

records.source: לֹ֥א תֹאכַ֖ל כָּל־תּוֹעֵבָֽה׃
records.gloss: Not you will eat any abomination.
pieces: Do not eat anything detestable.

L.3: You shall not eat any abomination.

decisions.choice: abomination: something the LORD detests and will not accept
decisions.reason: This is the word used for the gods and worship of the nations (7:25-26; 12:31), for dishonest weights (25:16) and for certain acts in Leviticus 18:22. Leviticus 11 uses a different word, "detestable", for forbidden creatures. Here the stronger word sums up all the foods forbidden in verses 4-21: to eat them would be to take into oneself what God rejects.

decisions.choice: you shall not eat: a heading for the list that follows
decisions.reason: The short command stands at the head of the food laws. Verses 4-21 then say which land animals, water creatures and flying creatures may and may not be eaten, in the same order as Leviticus 11.

decisions.choice: anything detestable / anything disgusting
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "abomination". Balanced says "detestable" and Readable "disgusting", the wording Leviticus 18:22 uses for this word.

records.heading: Clean and unclean food

records.source: זֹ֥את הַבְּהֵמָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר תֹּאכֵ֑לוּ שׁ֕וֹר שֵׂ֥ה כְשָׂבִ֖ים וְשֵׂ֥ה עִזִּֽים׃
records.gloss: This [is] the animal which you will eat: ox, sheep of lambs and sheep of goats,
pieces: These are the animals you may eat: the ox, the sheep and the goat,

L.4: This [is] the animal that you may eat: ox, one of [the] sheep, and one of [the] goats,

R.4: Here are the animals you may eat: cattle, sheep, goats,

decisions.choice: ox, sheep, goat: the domestic animals of Israel's herds and flocks
decisions.reason: These are the three kinds of livestock that Israel kept and offered in sacrifice (Leviticus 1:2-10; 22:27). The word used twice here means one animal of the flock, and can be a sheep or a goat (Exodus 12:5); each is defined by the word that follows it.

decisions.choice: this is the animal that you may eat: the permitted animals are named first
decisions.reason: Leviticus 11:2-3 first gives the two marks of a clean animal and then the exceptions. Deuteronomy first names ten clean animals, tame and wild (verses 4-5), and then gives the marks (verse 6). "You may eat" gives permission, as in Leviticus 11:2.

decisions.choice: the list runs on to verse 5
decisions.reason: The list of animals continues into verse 5, so verse 4 ends with a comma. Balanced and Readable use plurals for the singular collective "animal".

records.source: אַיָּ֥ל וּצְבִ֖י וְיַחְמ֑וּר וְאַקּ֥וֹ וְדִישֹׁ֖ן וּתְא֥וֹ וָזָֽמֶר׃
records.gloss: deer, and gazelle, and roebuck, and wild goat, and ibex, and antelope, and mountain sheep.
pieces: the deer, the gazelle, the roe deer, the wild goat, the ibex, the antelope and the mountain sheep.

L.5: deer, and gazelle, and roe deer, and wild goat, and ibex, and antelope, and mountain sheep.

R.5: deer, gazelles, roe deer, wild goats, ibex, antelope and mountain sheep.

decisions.choice: deer and gazelle: wild animals hunted for food
decisions.reason: The deer and the gazelle were the best-known game animals, hunted and eaten but not offered in sacrifice (12:15, 22; 15:22; 1 Kings 5:3). Their presence in this list shows that the clean animals include wild ones as well as livestock.

decisions.choice: roe deer, wild goat, ibex, antelope, mountain sheep: probable identifications
decisions.reason: Several of these names occur only here or very rarely, so they are identified from related words and ancient translations. The third may be a kind of deer (1 Kings 5:3). The fourth is probably a wild goat, and the fifth a mountain goat such as the ibex. The sixth is an animal caught in nets (Isaiah 51:20), perhaps an antelope or a wild ox. The seventh is probably a wild sheep. All are animals with split hooves that chew the cud, as verse 6 requires.

records.source: וְכָל־בְּהֵמָ֞ה מַפְרֶ֣סֶת פַּרְסָ֗ה וְשֹׁסַ֤עַת שֶׁ֨סַע֙ שְׁתֵּ֣י פְרָס֔וֹת מַעֲלַ֥ת גֵּרָ֖ה בַּבְּהֵמָ֑ה אֹתָ֖הּ תֹּאכֵֽלוּ׃
records.gloss: And every animal dividing [a] hoof and cleaving [a] cleft of two hooves, bringing up cud among the animals, it you will eat.
pieces: You may eat any animal that both chews the cud and has a hoof split fully into two.

L.6: And any animal that divides the hoof and is split [with] a cleft into two hooves, [and] brings up the cud, among the animals, it you may eat.

R.6: You may eat any animal that chews the cud and also has hooves that are split into two parts.

decisions.choice: divides the hoof and is split with a cleft into two hooves: the hoof is split completely into two toes
decisions.reason: As in Leviticus 11:3, two phrases say the same thing, and here the Hebrew adds "two hooves": the split goes all the way through, so that the foot has two separate toes. Cattle, sheep, goats and deer have such hooves; the horse, with a single solid hoof, does not.

decisions.choice: brings up the cud: chews again food brought back up from the stomach
decisions.reason: An animal that is to be eaten must have both signs, the split hoof and the chewing of the cud (Leviticus 11:3). Verses 7-8 give examples of animals with only one.

decisions.choice: chews the cud
decisions.reason: As in Leviticus 11:3, Literal keeps "brings up the cud" and Balanced and Readable use the usual expression "chews the cud".

records.source: אַ֣ךְ אֶת־זֶ֞ה לֹ֤א תֹֽאכְלוּ֙ מִמַּֽעֲלֵ֣י הַגֵּרָ֔ה וּמִמַּפְרִיסֵ֥י הַפַּרְסָ֖ה הַשְּׁסוּעָ֑ה אֶֽת־הַ֠גָּמָל וְאֶת־הָאַרְנֶ֨בֶת וְאֶת־הַשָּׁפָ֜ן כִּֽי־מַעֲלֵ֧ה גֵרָ֣ה הֵ֗מָּה וּפַרְסָה֙ לֹ֣א הִפְרִ֔יסוּ טְמֵאִ֥ים הֵ֖ם לָכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Nevertheless this not you will eat from [those] bringing up the cud and from [those] dividing the hoof [that is] cloven: the camel, and the hare, and the rock badger, for bringing up cud [are] they, and [a] hoof not they divide; unclean [are] they to you.
pieces: Yet you must not eat these, even though they chew the cud or have split hooves: the camel, the hare and the rock badger. They chew the cud but do not have split hooves, so they are unclean for you.

L.7: Nevertheless, these you shall not eat, of those that bring up the cud or of those that divide the hoof [and are] cloven: the camel, and the hare, and the rock badger, for they bring up the cud, but the hoof they do not divide; they [are] unclean to you.

R.7: But do not eat the animals that have only one of the two signs. The camel, the hare and the rock badger chew the cud, but their hooves are not split. So they are unclean for you.

decisions.choice: unclean: ritually impure, forbidden as food to Israel
decisions.reason: Unclean is not the same as dirty or sinful. It is a state that God's law assigns to certain animals, bodies and objects, and its opposite is clean (Leviticus 10:10; 11:4, 47). These animals are unclean "to you": forbidden to Israel as food. Living camels could still be ridden and handled. See Leviticus 11:4.

decisions.choice: rock badger: probably the rock hyrax, a small animal that lives among rocks
decisions.reason: As in Leviticus 11:5. The animal lives among the rocks (Psalm 104:18; Proverbs 30:26), which fits the rock hyrax, a small furry animal about the size of a rabbit. It is not a true badger. The identification is widely accepted, though not certain.

decisions.choice: the camel, the hare and the rock badger: each has only one of the two signs
decisions.reason: A camel's foot has two toes resting on a broad, soft pad, not two separate hard hooves. The hare and the hyrax do not have the several stomachs of cattle and sheep, but they move their jaws constantly as if chewing; the law describes them as an observer sees them (Leviticus 11:4-6). Deuteronomy names the hare before the rock badger; Leviticus has the reverse order.

decisions.choice: unclean for you
decisions.reason: As in Leviticus 11:4, "to you" means as far as you are concerned, for your eating, and Balanced and Readable say "for you".

records.source: וְאֶת־הַ֠חֲזִיר כִּֽי־מַפְרִ֨יס פַּרְסָ֥ה הוּא֙ וְלֹ֣א גֵרָ֔ה טָמֵ֥א ה֖וּא לָכֶ֑ם מִבְּשָׂרָם֙ לֹ֣א תֹאכֵ֔לוּ וּבְנִבְלָתָ֖ם לֹ֥א תִגָּֽעוּ׃ס
records.gloss: And the pig, for dividing [a] hoof [is] it, and not cud; unclean [is] it to you; from their meat not you will eat, and their carcass not you will touch.
pieces: The pig has split hooves but does not chew the cud; it is unclean for you. Do not eat any of their meat, and do not touch them when they are dead.

L.8: And the pig, for it divides the hoof, but [chews] no cud; it [is] unclean to you. Of their meat you shall not eat, and their carcass you shall not touch.

R.8: The pig has split hooves, but it does not chew the cud. So it is unclean for you. Do not eat the meat of any of these animals. Do not touch their bodies after they have died.

decisions.choice: the pig: an animal with split hooves that does not chew the cud
decisions.reason: The pig is named with the opposite lack to the camel, hare and rock badger (Leviticus 11:7). Later Scripture treats eating pork as a mark of turning away from God (Isaiah 65:4; 66:17).

decisions.choice: and not cud: it does not chew the cud
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is very short here, "and not cud", with no verb. Leviticus 11:7 gives the full phrase, "it does not chew the cud", and the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: their meat ... their carcass: of all four animals of verses 7-8, when dead
decisions.reason: "Their" covers the camel, the hare, the rock badger and the pig. The carcass is the body of an animal that has died or been killed; touching it made a person unclean (Leviticus 11:8, 24-28). The ban concerns these animals when dead, not the living camel.

decisions.choice: when they are dead / of any of these animals ... after they have died
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "when they are dead" for "their carcass", as in Leviticus 11:8, and Readable makes clear that "their" means all the animals just named.

records.source: אֶת־זֶה֙ תֹּֽאכְל֔וּ מִכֹּ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּמָּ֑יִם כֹּ֧ל אֲשֶׁר־ל֛וֹ סְנַפִּ֥יר וְקַשְׂקֶ֖שֶׂת תֹּאכֵֽלוּ׃
records.gloss: This you will eat from all which [is] in the waters: all which [belongs] to it fin and scale you will eat.
pieces: Among the creatures of the water, any that have fins and scales are yours to eat.

L.9: This you may eat of all that [is] in the waters: everything that has fin and scale you may eat.

R.9: You may eat water animals that have fins and scales.

decisions.choice: fin and scale: the two marks of water creatures that may be eaten
decisions.reason: As with land animals, a water creature must have both marks. Most fish have both; eels, catfish, shellfish and other sea creatures do not. Leviticus 11:9-12 gives the same rule at more length.

records.source: וְכֹ֨ל אֲשֶׁ֧ר אֵֽין־ל֛וֹ סְנַפִּ֥יר וְקַשְׂקֶ֖שֶׂת לֹ֣א תֹאכֵ֑לוּ טָמֵ֥א ה֖וּא לָכֶֽם׃ס
records.gloss: And all which there [is] not to it fin and scale not you will eat; unclean [is] it to you.
pieces: But do not eat anything without fins and scales; it is unclean for you.

L.10: And all that does not have fin and scale you shall not eat; it [is] unclean to you.

R.10: But do not eat water animals without fins and scales. They are unclean for you.

decisions.choice: unclean: forbidden as food
decisions.reason: Leviticus 11:10-12 calls such water creatures "detestable"; Deuteronomy uses "unclean", the word it uses for all the forbidden animals. The rule is the same.

decisions.choice: water animals
decisions.reason: Readable repeats "water animals" from verse 9, so that the short rule cannot be taken to cover land animals too.

records.source: כָּל־צִפּ֥וֹר טְהֹרָ֖ה תֹּאכֵֽלוּ׃
records.gloss: Every bird clean you will eat.
pieces: You may eat any clean bird.

L.11: Every clean bird you may eat.

R.11: You may eat any bird that is clean.

decisions.choice: clean bird: any bird not named in the list of verses 12-18
decisions.reason: No marks are given for birds as they are for land animals and fish. Instead the law names the forbidden birds, so every other bird is clean. The word for "bird" here is the common word for a small bird, often a sparrow-like bird. Doves and pigeons were offered in sacrifice (Leviticus 1:14), and quail were eaten in the wilderness (Exodus 16:13).

records.source: וְזֶ֕ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־תֹאכְל֖וּ מֵהֶ֑ם הַנֶּ֥שֶׁר וְהַפֶּ֖רֶס וְהָֽעָזְנִיָּֽה׃
records.gloss: And this [is that] which not you will eat of them: the eagle, and the bearded vulture, and the black vulture,
pieces: But these are the ones you must not eat: the eagle, the bearded vulture, the black vulture,

L.12: But this [is what] you shall not eat of them: the eagle, and the bearded vulture, and the black vulture,

R.12: But do not eat these birds: the eagle, the bearded vulture, the black vulture,

decisions.choice: the birds of verses 12-18: names whose exact identity is often uncertain
decisions.reason: As in Leviticus 11:13-19, the list gives names, not marks. Many of the names occur only in these two lists, so their identification rests on context, ancient translations and the meaning of the words. Most of those that can be identified are birds of prey, carrion eaters, or birds of marsh and ruin. The two lists match closely; Deuteronomy differs mainly in verse 13 and in the order of a few owls. The names in this translation are the best identifications, not certainties.

decisions.choice: eagle: a large bird of prey, possibly the griffon vulture
decisions.reason: As in Leviticus 11:13. The word is usually the eagle, but it can include the great vultures: Micah 1:16 speaks of baldness like that of this bird, which fits the griffon vulture's bare head.

decisions.choice: the list runs on to verse 18
decisions.reason: The list of birds is one sentence from verse 12 to verse 18, so verses 12-17 end with a comma, as in Leviticus 11:13-18.

records.source: וְהָרָאָה֙ וְאֶת־הָ֣אַיָּ֔ה וְהַדַּיָּ֖ה לְמִינָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: and the kite, and the black kite, and the kite after its kind,
pieces: the red kite, the black kite, the various kinds of kite,

L.13: and the red kite, and the black kite, and the kite after its kind,

R.13: the red kite, the black kite, all other kinds of kites,

decisions.choice: the red kite: probably the same bird as the first name in Leviticus 11:14
decisions.reason: This name occurs only here. In the same place Leviticus 11:14 has a word that differs from it by one letter, and the two Hebrew letters look much alike, so this is probably the same name changed in copying. The third name in this verse comes from the same root as the name in Leviticus, and may preserve another form of it; ancient copies and translations differ in this verse. Reviewers should check the evidence before this sentence is marked reviewed.

decisions.choice: red kite, black kite, kite: birds of prey that hunt and scavenge
decisions.reason: The second name is a keen-sighted bird of prey (Job 28:7) and is the black kite of Leviticus 11:14. The third, found also in Isaiah 34:15, probably comes from a verb for swooping or darting. All three are probably kites or birds like them, but this is not certain.

decisions.choice: after its kind: including all the birds of that kind
decisions.reason: As in Leviticus 11:14, the phrase widens the name to the whole group of related birds.

decisions.choice: all other kinds of kites
decisions.reason: Readable adds "other" so that the third name does not seem to repeat the first two.

records.source: וְאֵ֥ת כָּל־עֹרֵ֖ב לְמִינֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: and every raven after its kind,
pieces: every kind of raven,

L.14: and every raven after its kind,

R.14: all kinds of ravens and crows,

decisions.choice: raven: the raven and the birds related to it
decisions.reason: As in Leviticus 11:15. The raven is a well-known bird (Genesis 8:7; 1 Kings 17:4-6), and "after its kind" includes the crows.

decisions.choice: ravens and crows
decisions.reason: As in Leviticus 11:15, Readable names the crow, the best-known bird of the raven's kind.

records.source: וְאֵת֙ בַּ֣ת הַֽיַּעֲנָ֔ה וְאֶת־הַתַּחְמָ֖ס וְאֶת־הַשָּׁ֑חַף וְאֶת־הַנֵּ֖ץ לְמִינֵֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: and the daughter of the ostrich, and the screech owl, and the gull, and the falcon after its kind,
pieces: the ostrich, the screech owl, the gull, the various kinds of falcon,

L.15: and the ostrich, and the screech owl, and the gull, and the falcon after its kind,

R.15: the ostrich, the screech owl, the seagull, all kinds of falcons,

decisions.choice: the ostrich: literally "the daughter of the desert bird", probably the ostrich
decisions.reason: As in Leviticus 11:16. The phrase is used of a bird of the desert and of ruins, known for its cry (Job 30:29; Isaiah 13:21; Micah 1:8). The ostrich fits, though some take it as a large owl.

decisions.choice: screech owl, gull, falcon: uncertain identifications
decisions.reason: As in Leviticus 11:16. The first name may come from a verb for violence or for robbing; the second from a word for thin or lean; the third, a bird of prey, is named in Job 39:26 for flying south. These identifications are probable, not certain.

records.source: אֶת־הַכּ֥וֹס וְאֶת־הַיַּנְשׁ֖וּף וְהַתִּנְשָֽׁמֶת׃
records.gloss: the little owl, and the great owl, and the barn owl,
pieces: the little owl, the eagle owl, the barn owl,

L.16: the little owl, and the eagle owl, and the barn owl,

R.16: the little owl, the eagle owl, the barn owl,

decisions.choice: little owl, eagle owl, barn owl: probable identifications
decisions.reason: The same three names are in Leviticus 11:17-18, in a different order. The first is an owl of ruins (Psalm 102:7). The second lives in ruined places (Isaiah 34:11) and is probably a large owl. The third may come from a verb for breathing or hissing. None of these is certain.

records.source: וְהַקָּאָ֥ת וְאֶֽת־הָרָחָ֖מָה וְאֶת־הַשָּׁלָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: and the desert owl, and the Egyptian vulture, and the cormorant,
pieces: the desert owl, the carrion vulture, the cormorant,

L.17: and the desert owl, and the carrion vulture, and the cormorant,

R.17: the desert owl, the vulture, the cormorant,

decisions.choice: desert owl, carrion vulture, cormorant: probable identifications
decisions.reason: The three names are in Leviticus 11:17-18. The first lives in deserts and ruins (Psalm 102:7; Isaiah 34:11). The second is a longer form of the name in Leviticus 11:18, from a root for tenderness, and is probably the small white Egyptian vulture, which feeds on carrion. The third comes from a verb meaning to throw down, which fits a bird that plunges after fish. None of these is certain.

records.source: וְהַ֣חֲסִידָ֔ה וְהָאֲנָפָ֖ה לְמִינָ֑הּ וְהַדּוּכִיפַ֖ת וְהָעֲטַלֵּֽף׃
records.gloss: and the stork, and the heron after its kind, and the hoopoe, and the bat.
pieces: the stork, the various kinds of heron, the hoopoe and the bat.

L.18: and the stork, and the heron after its kind, and the hoopoe, and the bat.

R.18: the stork, all kinds of herons, the hoopoe and the bat.

decisions.choice: stork, heron, hoopoe: birds known from their habits
decisions.reason: As in Leviticus 11:19. The stork nests in trees and migrates (Psalm 104:17; Jeremiah 8:7). The heron is less certain. The hoopoe is a crested bird that probes the ground and dung for insects.

decisions.choice: the bat: a flying creature, though not a bird
decisions.reason: As in Leviticus 11:19, the list is of flying creatures in general, so the bat can be named with them.

records.source: וְכֹל֙ שֶׁ֣רֶץ הָע֔וֹף טָמֵ֥א ה֖וּא לָכֶ֑ם לֹ֖א יֵאָכֵֽלוּ׃
records.gloss: And every swarming thing of the flying [kind], unclean [is] it to you; not they will be eaten.
pieces: All winged swarming creatures are unclean for you. They must not be eaten.

L.19: And every swarming thing that flies [is] unclean to you; they shall not be eaten.

R.19: All insects with wings are unclean for you. Do not eat them.

decisions.choice: every swarming thing that flies: winged insects
decisions.reason: The phrase is the one Leviticus 11:20-23 uses for winged insects. A swarming thing is a small creature that appears in great numbers (Genesis 1:20; Leviticus 11:10).

decisions.choice: unclean to you: no exception is given here
decisions.reason: Leviticus 11:21-22 allows four kinds of leaping insect, the locust, the bald locust, the cricket and the grasshopper. Deuteronomy does not repeat the exception. It gives the general rule, and verse 20 may leave room for the clean winged creatures of Leviticus; the text does not say whether locusts are meant to be included there.

decisions.choice: insects with wings
decisions.reason: As in Leviticus 11:20, Readable says "insects with wings" for "swarming things that fly".

records.source: כָּל־ע֥וֹף טָה֖וֹר תֹּאכֵֽלוּ׃
records.gloss: Every flying thing clean you will eat.
pieces: But you may eat any clean winged creature.

L.20: Every clean flying thing you may eat.

R.20: But you may eat any clean creature that flies.

decisions.choice: clean flying thing: any winged creature that is clean
decisions.reason: The word here is wider than the word for "bird" in verse 11. It means anything that flies, and it is the word used in verse 19 for winged insects. So the verse permits clean birds, and it may also include the leaping insects that Leviticus 11:21-22 allows (see verse 19).

decisions.choice: But
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no joining word. Balanced and Readable add "but" to show that this verse is set against verse 19.

records.source: לֹ֣א תֹאכְל֣וּ כָל־נְ֠בֵלָה לַגֵּ֨ר אֲשֶׁר־בִּשְׁעָרֶ֜יךָ תִּתְּנֶ֣נָּה וַאֲכָלָ֗הּ א֤וֹ מָכֹר֙ לְנָכְרִ֔י כִּ֣י עַ֤ם קָדוֹשׁ֙ אַתָּ֔ה לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ לֹֽא־תְבַשֵּׁ֥ל גְּדִ֖י בַּחֲלֵ֥ב אִמּֽוֹ׃פ
records.gloss: Not you will eat any carcass; to the sojourner who [is] in your gates you will give it, and he will eat it, or sell [it] to a foreigner; for a people holy [are] you to Yahweh your God. Not you will boil a kid in [the] milk of its mother.
pieces: Do not eat anything that has died on its own. The outsider living in your towns may have it to eat if you give it to them, or a foreigner may buy it from you. For you are a people set apart as holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. You shall not boil a young goat in its mother's milk.

L.21: You shall not eat any carcass. To the sojourner who [is] within your gates you may give it, and he may eat it, or [you may] sell [it] to a foreigner; for you [are] a holy people to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. You shall not boil a kid in its mother's milk.

R.21: Do not eat any animal that has died by itself. You may give it to an outsider who lives in your town, and they may eat it. Or you may sell it to someone from another country. This is because you belong to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God as a holy people. Do not cook a young goat in milk from its own mother.

decisions.choice: carcass: an animal that has died of itself, not slaughtered
decisions.reason: Such an animal was not slaughtered, so its blood was not drained out (12:16, 23; Leviticus 17:10-15). Leviticus treats eating it as making a person unclean until evening (Leviticus 11:39-40; 17:15). Deuteronomy forbids Israel to eat it at all, because Israel is a holy people, as priests are forbidden in Leviticus 22:8.

decisions.choice: the sojourner and the foreigner: an outsider living in Israel, and a foreigner from abroad
decisions.reason: The sojourner is an outsider who has settled among Israel without land or family rights, often poor, and Israel is to provide for him (10:18-19; 14:29). The foreigner is someone from another people, such as a trader passing through (15:3; 23:21). So the meat may be given to the one and sold to the other. Neither belongs to the holy people, and the rule binds only Israel.

decisions.choice: do not boil a young goat in its mother's milk: the reason is uncertain
decisions.reason: The law is given three times (Exodus 23:19; 34:26; and here) with no reason stated. It may forbid a practice of other peoples' worship, or it may teach respect for the bond between mother and young, like Leviticus 22:28 and Deuteronomy 22:6-7. Here it closes the food laws. Later Jewish tradition built on it the practice of keeping meat and milk apart.

decisions.choice: for you are a holy people: the reason, as in verse 2
decisions.reason: The words of verse 2 are repeated to close the food laws: Israel's food is different because Israel belongs to the LORD.

decisions.choice: outsider living in your towns; foreigner / someone from another country
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "sojourner" and "within your gates". Balanced and Readable say "outsider", as in Leviticus 19:33, so that it is not confused with the "foreigner" in the same verse, and "in your towns" for "in your gates", since a town's gate stands for the town (Exodus 20:10).

decisions.choice: anything that has died on its own / any animal that has died by itself
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "carcass" means here, as Leviticus 11:39 does.

records.source: עַשֵּׂ֣ר תְּעַשֵּׂ֔ר אֵ֖ת כָּל־תְּבוּאַ֣ת זַרְעֶ֑ךָ הַיֹּצֵ֥א הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה שָׁנָ֥ה שָׁנָֽה׃
records.gloss: Surely you will tithe all [the] produce of your seed which comes out [of] the field year [by] year.
pieces: Year after year, be sure to set aside a tithe of all the crops that grow from the seed you sow in the field.

L.22: You shall surely tithe all the produce of your seed that comes out of the field year by year.

R.22: Every year, be sure to set aside a tenth of all the crops that grow in your fields.

decisions.choice: you shall surely tithe: the verb is doubled for emphasis
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats the verb, "tithing you shall tithe", to stress that the tithe must not be neglected.

decisions.choice: tithe: a tenth of the yearly harvest, eaten by the giver at the sanctuary
decisions.reason: The word means to give a tenth. Leviticus 27:30-32 says the tithe belongs to the LORD, and Numbers 18:21-24 gives it to the Levites for their service. Here the tithe of the harvest is brought to the sanctuary and eaten there by the family that gives it, with the Levite sharing in it (verses 23-27). The law does not explain how these rules fit together. They may describe one tithe from different sides, or two different tithes, as later Jewish practice held.

decisions.choice: the produce of your seed that comes out of the field: the grain and other crops grown from sowing
decisions.reason: "Seed" here is what is sown and the harvest it yields. Verse 23 names the grain, the new wine and the oil.

decisions.choice: a tenth
decisions.reason: As in Leviticus 27:30, Readable says what "tithe" means; Literal and Balanced keep the word.

records.heading: The yearly tithe

records.source: וְאָכַלְתָּ֞ לִפְנֵ֣י׀יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֗יךָ בַּמָּק֣וֹם אֲשֶׁר־יִבְחַר֮ לְשַׁכֵּ֣ן שְׁמ֣וֹ שָׁם֒ מַעְשַׂ֤ר דְּגָֽנְךָ֙ תִּֽירֹשְׁךָ֣ וְיִצְהָרֶ֔ךָ וּבְכֹרֹ֥ת בְּקָרְךָ֖ וְצֹאנֶ֑ךָ לְמַ֣עַן תִּלְמַ֗ד לְיִרְאָ֛ה אֶת־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ כָּל־הַיָּמִֽים׃
records.gloss: And you will eat before Yahweh your God in the place which he will choose to cause to dwell his name there, [the] tithe of your grain, your new wine and your fresh oil, and [the] firstborn of your herd and your flock, so that you may learn to fear Yahweh your God all the days.
pieces: Eat it before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, in the place {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chooses as a dwelling for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name: the tithe of your grain, your new wine and your olive oil, and the firstborn of your cattle and your flocks. In this way you will learn to fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God at all times.

L.23: And you shall eat before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, in the place where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chooses to make {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name dwell, the tithe of your grain, your new wine and your fresh oil, and the firstborn of your herd and your flock, so that you may learn to fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God all the days.

R.23: Bring the tenth of your grain, your new wine and your olive oil, and the firstborn animals of your cattle, sheep and goats, to the place that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will choose as the home for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name. Eat them there in the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. Then you will learn to fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God all your life.

decisions.choice: the place he chooses to make his name dwell: the one sanctuary God will choose in the land
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 12 commands Israel to bring its offerings and tithes only to the place God will choose, and not to worship wherever it likes (12:5, 11, 14, 18). The place is not named; later it is Jerusalem and its temple (1 Kings 8:29; 11:36). God's "name" stands for God himself as he makes himself known: where his name dwells, he is present and the place is his.

decisions.choice: grain, new wine, fresh oil: the three main crops of the land
decisions.reason: The three often go together as the gifts of the land (7:13; 11:14; 12:17). The new wine is the fresh juice of the grape harvest, and the oil is fresh olive oil.

decisions.choice: the firstborn of your herd and your flock: male firstborn animals, which belong to the LORD
decisions.reason: Every firstborn male of the herd and flock belongs to the LORD (Exodus 13:2, 12; Deuteronomy 15:19-20). Like the tithe, it is eaten by the family at the sanctuary.

decisions.choice: learn to fear the LORD: to grow in reverent awe and obedience
decisions.reason: To fear the LORD is to honor him with awe and to do what he says (4:10; 6:2, 24; 10:12). The joyful meal at God's place, year after year, teaches it.

decisions.choice: Bring ... Eat them there
decisions.reason: Readable puts the gifts first and divides the long sentence. It adds "Bring", which the Hebrew implies, since the tithe must be carried to the place (verse 24).

decisions.choice: olive oil
decisions.reason: Literal says "fresh oil". Balanced and Readable say "olive oil", which the word means.

records.source: וְכִֽי־יִרְבֶּ֨ה מִמְּךָ֜ הַדֶּ֗רֶךְ כִּ֣י לֹ֣א תוּכַ֘לשְׂאֵתוֹ֒ כִּֽי־יִרְחַ֤ק מִמְּךָ֙ הַמָּק֔וֹם אֲשֶׁ֤ר יִבְחַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ לָשׂ֥וּם שְׁמ֖וֹ שָׁ֑ם כִּ֥י יְבָרֶכְךָ֖ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And if is too great for you the way, that not you are able to carry it, for is too far from you the place which will choose Yahweh your God to set his name there, for will bless you Yahweh your God,
pieces: If the journey is too long for you and you cannot carry it, because the place where {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God chooses to put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name is too far from you, when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has blessed you with plenty,

L.24: And if the way is too long for you, so that you are not able to carry it, because the place that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God chooses to put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name there is too far from you, when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God blesses you,

R.24: But the place that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God chooses for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name may be too far away from you. When {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God blesses you with large harvests, you may not be able to carry your tenth that far.

decisions.choice: when the LORD your God blesses you: the large harvest that makes the tithe too heavy to carry
alternatives: because the LORD your God has blessed you
decisions.reason: The joining word can mean "when" or "because". Either way, the blessing of a good harvest makes the tithe large, and a long journey would make it hard to carry.

decisions.choice: to set his name there: the same as "to make his name dwell there"
decisions.reason: The two phrases are used side by side for the chosen place (12:5, 21).

decisions.choice: with plenty / with large harvests
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the blessing is here, since it explains why the tithe is too much to carry.

decisions.choice: two sentences
decisions.reason: Readable puts the distance first and makes two sentences, ending the condition here; verse 25 then begins a new sentence. Literal and Balanced keep the one sentence running into verse 25 and end with a comma.

records.source: וְנָתַתָּ֖ה בַּכָּ֑סֶף וְצַרְתָּ֤ הַכֶּ֨סֶף֙ בְּיָ֣דְךָ֔ וְהָֽלַכְתָּ֙ אֶל־הַמָּק֔וֹם אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִבְחַ֛ר יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ בּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: and you will give [it] for money, and you will bind up the money in your hand, and you will go to the place which will choose Yahweh your God in it.
pieces: then turn it into money. Tie up the money and carry it with you to the place {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God chooses.

L.25: then you shall exchange [it] for money, and bind up the money in your hand, and go to the place that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God chooses.

R.25: Then sell it and take the money with you. Go to the place that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God chooses.

decisions.choice: money ... bind up the money in your hand: silver tied in a bag and carried
decisions.reason: The word for money is "silver". There were no coins yet; silver was weighed out, and it was carried tied in a bag or cloth (Genesis 42:35; 2 Kings 5:23). The worshiper takes the value of the tithe instead of the tithe itself.

decisions.choice: give for money: exchange the produce for silver
decisions.reason: The verb "give" with "for" means to give one thing in exchange for another, here to sell the tithe at home.

decisions.choice: chooses: the Hebrew ends "chooses in it"
decisions.reason: In Hebrew the place is chosen "in it", which simply points back to "the place" and adds nothing to the sense.

decisions.choice: sell it
decisions.reason: Readable says "sell it" for "give it for money".

records.source: וְנָתַתָּ֣ה הַכֶּ֡סֶף בְּכֹל֩ אֲשֶׁר־תְּאַוֶּ֨ה נַפְשְׁךָ֜ בַּבָּקָ֣ר וּבַצֹּ֗אן וּבַיַּ֨יִן֙ וּבַשֵּׁכָ֔ר וּבְכֹ֛ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר תִּֽשְׁאָלְךָ֖ נַפְשֶׁ֑ךָ וְאָכַ֣לְתָּ שָּׁ֗ם לִפְנֵי֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ וְשָׂמַחְתָּ֖ אַתָּ֥ה וּבֵיתֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And you will give the money for all that desires your soul, for cattle and for sheep and for wine and for strong drink and for all that asks you your soul, and you will eat there before Yahweh your God, and you will rejoice, you and your household.
pieces: Spend the money on whatever you wish: cattle, sheep, wine, beer, or anything else you would like. Then eat there in the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and rejoice, you and your household.

L.26: And you shall spend the money on anything that your soul desires, on cattle or on sheep or on wine or on strong drink, or on anything that your soul asks of you; and you shall eat there before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and rejoice, you and your household.

R.26: Use the money to buy anything you like: cattle, sheep, wine, beer or anything else you want. Then you and your family are to eat there in the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and be glad together.

decisions.choice: your soul desires ... your soul asks: whatever you long for, your appetite
decisions.reason: The word often rendered "soul" here means a person's appetite and desire, as in 12:15, 20-21. The family may buy whatever it likes for the feast.

decisions.choice: wine and strong drink: wine and other fermented drink, such as beer
decisions.reason: As in Leviticus 10:9, the second word means an intoxicating drink other than wine, most likely beer made from grain. Here both are part of a joyful feast before God, as wine elsewhere is a gift that gladdens (Psalm 104:15).

decisions.choice: eat before the LORD and rejoice: a joyful meal of worship
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy often joins eating at the chosen place with rejoicing before the LORD (12:7, 12, 18; 16:11). The tithe is not only a duty but a feast of thanks for the harvest. The household includes children and servants (12:18).

decisions.choice: beer
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "strong drink". Balanced and Readable say "beer", as in Leviticus 10:9.

decisions.choice: whatever you wish / anything you like
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "your soul desires". Balanced and Readable use plain words for what you want.

records.source: וְהַלֵּוִ֥י אֲשֶׁר־בִּשְׁעָרֶ֖יךָ לֹ֣א תַֽעַזְבֶ֑נּוּ כִּ֣י אֵ֥ין ל֛וֹ חֵ֥לֶק וְנַחֲלָ֖ה עִמָּֽךְ׃ס
records.gloss: And the Levite who [is] in your gates, not you will forsake him, for there [is] not to him portion and inheritance with you.
pieces: And do not neglect the Levite living in your towns, since he has no portion or inheritance among you.

L.27: And the Levite who [is] within your gates, you shall not forsake him, for he has no portion or inheritance with you.

R.27: Do not forget about the Levites who live in your towns. They do not have their own land as you do.

decisions.choice: the Levite within your gates: a member of the tribe of Levi, living in the towns of Israel
decisions.reason: The tribe of Levi received no territory of its own but lived scattered in towns among the other tribes (Numbers 35:1-8). The Levites lived from the tithes and offerings given to the LORD (10:9; 18:1-2; Numbers 18:21-24), so they depended on the people's faithfulness.

decisions.choice: you shall not forsake him: do not leave him without support
decisions.reason: The verb means to leave or abandon. Here it means to leave the Levite out of the tithe meal; 12:12, 18-19 says the same.

decisions.choice: portion and inheritance: a share of the land passed down in the family
decisions.reason: As in Numbers 18:20, the pair means a family's share of land. The LORD is the Levites' inheritance instead (10:9; 18:2).

decisions.choice: their own land as you do
decisions.reason: Readable explains "portion and inheritance" as land, and uses the plural for the Levites as a group.

records.source: מִקְצֵ֣ה׀שָׁלֹ֣שׁ שָׁנִ֗ים תּוֹצִיא֙ אֶת־כָּל־מַעְשַׂר֙ תְּבוּאָ֣תְךָ֔ בַּשָּׁנָ֖ה הַהִ֑וא וְהִנַּחְתָּ֖ בִּשְׁעָרֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: At [the] end of three years you will bring out all [the] tithe of your produce in the year the that, and you will deposit [it] in your gates.
pieces: At the end of every third year, bring out the whole tithe of that year's produce and store it in your towns.

L.28: At the end of three years you shall bring out all the tithe of your produce in that year and lay [it] up within your gates.

R.28: Every third year, bring the whole tenth of that year's crops and store it in your own town.

decisions.choice: at the end of three years ... in that year: in every third year, the tithe stays in the towns
decisions.reason: In 26:12 the third year is called "the year of the tithe". In that year the tithe is not taken to the sanctuary but stored in the towns for those who have no land. Jewish practice later kept this tithe for the poor in the third and sixth years of each seven-year cycle. The phrase "at the end of" means at the close of the third year's harvest, or in the course of that year; 15:1 uses a similar phrase for the seventh year.

decisions.choice: bring out ... lay it up: gather it from the fields and store it locally
decisions.reason: The first verb is to bring out the produce from the fields and storerooms; the second is to set it down and leave it, here in a store in the town.

decisions.choice: every third year
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "every", since the rule repeats; Literal keeps "at the end of three years".

records.heading: The tithe of the third year

records.source: וּבָ֣א הַלֵּוִ֡י כִּ֣י אֵֽין־לוֹ֩ חֵ֨לֶק וְנַחֲלָ֜ה עִמָּ֗ךְ וְ֠הַגֵּר וְהַיָּת֤וֹם וְהָֽאַלְמָנָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בִּשְׁעָרֶ֔יךָ וְאָכְל֖וּ וְשָׂבֵ֑עוּ לְמַ֤עַן יְבָרֶכְךָ֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ בְּכָל־מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יָדְךָ֖ אֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּעֲשֶֽׂה׃ס
records.gloss: And will come the Levite, for there [is] not to him portion and inheritance with you, and the sojourner and the fatherless and the widow who [are] in your gates, and they will eat and be satisfied, so that will bless you Yahweh your God in all [the] work of your hand which you will do.
pieces: Then the Levite, who has no portion or inheritance among you, and the outsider, the fatherless and the widow who live in your towns may come and eat until they are full, so that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God may bless you in all the work you do.

L.29: And the Levite shall come, for he has no portion or inheritance with you, and the sojourner and the fatherless and the widow who [are] within your gates, and they shall eat and be satisfied, so that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God may bless you in all the work of your hand that you do.

R.29: Then the Levites, the outsiders, the children without fathers and the widows in your town can come and eat all they want. The Levites have no land of their own as you do. If you do this, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will bless you in all the work you do.

decisions.choice: the Levite, the sojourner, the fatherless and the widow: those without land or a provider
decisions.reason: The Levite has no land; the sojourner is an outsider without land or family rights; the fatherless child and the widow have lost the man who provided for them. God takes up their cause (10:18-19), and Deuteronomy often names them together as those Israel must feed and include (16:11, 14; 24:19-21; 26:12-13).

decisions.choice: eat and be satisfied: eat their fill
decisions.reason: The verb means to have enough and more. The poor are not given scraps but a full meal, as Israel itself will eat and be satisfied in the land (6:11; 8:10).

decisions.choice: so that the LORD your God may bless you: generosity and blessing go together
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy ties care for the poor to God's blessing on the work of those who give (15:10; 24:19). The blessing is not a payment earned but God's answer to a people who share what he has given them.

decisions.choice: outsider; the fatherless / children without fathers
decisions.reason: As in verse 21, Balanced and Readable say "outsider" for the sojourner. Readable says "children without fathers" for "the fatherless", as Exodus 22:21 explains the word.

decisions.choice: The Levites have no land of their own as you do.
decisions.reason: Readable moves the reason about the Levites into a sentence of its own, so the list of those who come is easier to follow, and says "If you do this" for "so that".
